tour1_body:
HaulNX is a ROM management app for your Switch. Organize your library by console, verify files are good, and keep your emulators pointed at the right folders. You can also browse curated archive.org collections to fill gaps with legitimate homebrew, public-domain, and preservation content.

This quick tour covers the essentials. Replay it any time from Settings > Help.
tour2_body:
Library is your management home: every installed game, grouped by console, with Verify, Tidy, and box art tools.

Switch between tabs with L/R, or the tab bar at the top.
tour8_body:
Collections lists every console HaulNX supports. Each one can point at one or more repositories you can browse: curated sources for legitimate homebrew, public-domain, and preservation content.

Press X on a console, then Add Repo, to add one by archive.org item ID or a direct URL.
tour3_body:
Pick a console then a repository to see its files. Press X to select several at once, then A to queue everything you picked in one go.

Queued items download in the background, so you're free to keep browsing while they run.
tour4_body: Queue lists every active and pending transfer in one place: downloads, files pushed from a PC, and app/emulator updates. Press A on an item to cancel it.
tour5_title: Point your emulators at your library
tour5_body:
Games install to sdmc:/roms/<console> by default. Most emulators need to be told to look there: set each emulator's ROM folder to match, or do the reverse and give a console its own custom install folder in Settings > Storage > Install Folders if an emulator expects its own path.

Get this right once and every future download just shows up.
tour6_body:
Settings > Data Files can verify your games against known-good checksums (DAT files) and flag anything missing or corrupt. Settings > Storage lets you tidy up misfiled or duplicate files, console by console.

Box art, card vs. list view, and what's using your SD card space all live in Appearance and Storage too.
tour7_body:
The free HaulNX desktop app connects over Wi-Fi (via the always-on inventory server) or USB to move files both ways, back up your collection, and manage emulators, with no SD card shuffling.

Find it under Settings > PC Sync. And remember: Settings > Help has How-To guides and Troubleshooting whenever you need them.
gs1_body:
HaulNX is a ROM management app first, a downloader second: it organizes your installed games by console, verifies them against checksums, cleans up misfiled or duplicate files, fetches box art, and keeps emulators and apps updated.

Browsing curated archive.org repositories to fill gaps in your library is one part of that, not the whole app.
gs2_title: Point your emulators at your library
gs2_body:
By default, games install to sdmc:/roms/<console> — a plain folder per console (Settings > Storage shows the exact path). Set each emulator's ROM path to match, or use Settings > Storage > Install Folders to give a console its own custom path instead if an emulator expects one.

Do this once per emulator and new downloads just appear where it expects them.
gs3_body:
You need at least one repository before there's anything to browse.

From Add, press Y to add a repository, or use the desktop companion (Settings > PC Sync) to send a ready-made collection over Wi-Fi or USB.
gs4_body:
Downloaded archives extract straight into your ROM folder automatically, unless you turn on Keep Archives Compressed in Settings > Downloads.

Anything that lands without a clear match sits in the Inbox (Settings > Storage) until you sort it.
gs5_body:
Settings is organized by task: Appearance, Downloads, Storage, Data Files, PC Sync, Account, Updates, Logs, Diagnostics, and this Help section.

Each row opens a single-purpose screen — nothing is buried more than one level deep.
gs6_body:
Come back to Settings > Help any time: How-To covers everyday tasks like adding art or updating emulators, and Troubleshooting walks through common problems and fixes.

You can also replay the guided tour from the row above.
howto1_body:
From Add, press Y (or a console's Options menu) to add a repository by archive.org item ID or a direct download URL.

You can also use Search (the magnifying glass) to search archive.org's catalogue and add a matching item directly.
howto2_body:
In a repository's file list, press X on a file to select it, then keep selecting more — a running count and total size shows at the bottom. Press A once to queue everything selected together.

Settings > Downloads controls how many run at once and any rate limits, if downloads feel too fast or too slow.
howto3_title: Point your emulators at your ROM folder
howto3_body:
Games install to sdmc:/roms/<console> by default (Settings > Storage shows the exact path). Point each emulator's ROM folder setting there.

If an emulator insists on its own folder instead, turn on Settings > Storage > Install Folder Mode (custom) and set that one console's path under Console Folders — HaulNX will install there instead, no manual copying.
howto4_title: Download DAT files and verify your library
howto4_body:
Settings > Data Files > Manage DAT Files downloads the checksum sets used to verify games.

From a console's Options menu in Library, choose Verify Files to check every installed game against its DAT — bad, unknown, or misnamed files are listed with a fix offered where possible.
howto5_body: From a console's Options menu in Library, choose Tidy Library to scan for misfiled and duplicate files. Each finding lists a suggested fix — review one at a time, or apply everything at once.
howto6_title: Add box art for consoles and games
howto6_body:
From a console's Options menu in Library, choose Scan for Box Art to fetch covers for everything installed at once.

On a single game, open its Options menu and pick a cover manually if the automatic match isn't right, or if you just want a different one.
howto7_body:
Settings > Appearance switches between card and list view, groups games by console or shows them flat, and sets the accent color and light/dark theme.

Box Art and Auto-Fetch Box Art are separate toggles there too — turn either off if you'd rather keep things fast and plain.
howto8_body: Settings > Appearance > Language lists every language HaulNX ships with. Pick one and the whole app updates immediately — no restart needed.
howto9_body: Settings > Sources (or Appearance) > Manage Consoles lets you show or hide any console on Browse and Library independently — hide ones you don't use without deleting their repos or configuration.
howto10_body:
Settings > Updates > App & Emulator Updates lists everything with an update source configured, shows installed vs. latest version, and installs or reverts a build in place.

Set a source first (X on an entry) if one isn't configured yet.
howto11_body: Settings > Storage > DAT Files hosts the 1G1R region-preference order — set which region wins when the same game exists in several regions, then Verify or Tidy applies it.
howto12_title: Move a game to another console folder
howto12_body: Open a game's Options menu (X) in Library and choose Move — pick the destination console and it's relocated (and re-verified if you have DATs for it).
howto13_title: Free up space: clear out folders
howto13_body:
Settings > Storage > Manage Downloads clears the scratch folder used mid-download; Manage Inbox clears anything that landed without a clear match.

Largest Files lists your whole library's biggest files first, so you know exactly what to remove if space is tight.
howto14_title: View logs and export a debug bundle
howto14_body:
Settings > Logs holds the download history, debug log, queue state, transfer log, and speed-test log — each viewable and clearable on its own.

Export Debug Bundle folds all of them into one file to attach to a bug report.
howto15_title: Connect the PC companion over Wi-Fi
howto15_body: Turn on the inventory server in Settings > PC Sync, then open the HaulNX desktop app on the same network — it finds your console automatically and can push or pull files, back up your collection, and manage emulators, all without a cable.
howto16_body: Settings > Diagnostics > USB File Transfer turns your console into a USB drive the desktop app (or any MTP-capable file manager) can browse and transfer to — cable-only, no Wi-Fi needed.
howto17_body: The magnifying glass in Library searches installed games; in Add it searches across every repository you've added; and in a console's file list it searches archive.org's catalogue for that console.
howto18_title: Back up and restore your collection setup
howto18_body: HaulNX automatically keeps the last two versions of your console/repository configuration. Settings > PC Sync > Restore Collection brings one back if an import or edit went wrong.
howto19_body:
By default, a downloaded archive (zip/rar/7z) extracts straight into the right console folder automatically and the archive itself is deleted once it lands — you never handle a zip file by hand.

Turn on Keep Archives Compressed (Settings > Downloads) to keep new downloads zipped instead, trading a bit of convenience for less used space and a slightly longer install step in your emulator.

Anything that finishes downloading but doesn't clearly match a console sits in the Inbox (Settings > Storage) unextracted until you sort it by hand.
howto20_title: Add your Archive.org, GitHub, and SteamGridDB credentials
howto20_body:
Settings > Account Credentials holds three separate, optional pieces of login:

• Archive.org Access/Secret Key — needed only for items that require a logged-in archive.org account to download. Generate a pair at archive.org/account/s3.php and enter both under Archive.org Credentials.

• GitHub API Token — raises how often HaulNX can check GitHub for emulator/app/DAT updates before being rate-limited. A free personal access token with no special scopes is enough; generate one at github.com/settings/tokens.

• SteamGridDB API Key — lets box-art scans pull higher-quality art. Get a free key at steamgriddb.com/profile/preferences/api.

All three are stored on the console and never required just to browse or download public items.
howto21_body:
Appearance — theme, accent color, card vs. list view, box art.
Downloads — extraction, rate limits, keep-archives-compressed, inbox handling.
Filters — which file types repositories show.
Storage — free space, biggest folders, custom console install folders.
PC Sync — the desktop companion: Wi-Fi/USB transfer, install from PC, restore a backed-up collection.
Account Credentials — optional Archive.org/GitHub/SteamGridDB logins (see the credentials article).
Updates — check for and install HaulNX, emulator, and app updates.
Data Files — download DAT sets used by Verify.
Logs / Diagnostics — activity log, network self-test, USB transfer toggle, debug bundle export.
Help — this hub, and the guided tour.
howto22_title: Set a custom install folder for a console
howto22_body:
Games install to sdmc:/roms/<console> by default. If an emulator expects its own path instead, open Settings > Storage > Install Folders and switch it from Default to Custom Per Console, then pick the console and choose any folder on the SD card as its install location.

Verify, Tidy, and box art all keep working normally against the new folder. The change only applies to new downloads; anything already installed under the old path needs moving by hand.
howto23_body:
Settings > Downloads has three knobs for how downloads behave:

Max Simultaneous Downloads sets how many run at once (higher isn't always faster on a slow connection).
Max Total Download Rate caps combined throughput across every active download.
Max Rate Per Download caps each one individually, useful for keeping one big download from starving the others.

All three default to unlimited/1. Set any rate to 0 to remove that cap.
howto24_title: Hide file types you don't want to see
howto24_body:
Open Settings > Appearance > File Extension Filter to hide specific file types from repository listings and downloads, such as extras, artwork, or manuals that sometimes ship alongside a ROM.

Toggle the master switch on, then add an extension (Y) and toggle it on to start hiding it. Turning an individual extension off keeps it in the list without hiding it, so you can re-enable it later without re-adding it.
ts1_body:
HaulNX warns if it can't reach the internet when it starts. Retry once you're connected, or Continue to browse anything already cached — downloading and browsing repositories both need a connection.

Turn this check off in Settings > Diagnostics if you often use HaulNX offline.
ts2_body:
Check Settings > Diagnostics > Network Self-Test for a quick connectivity check, and Speed Test to measure real throughput.

A download rate limit set too low (Settings > Downloads) can also look like a stall — try raising or clearing it.
ts3_title: The PC companion won't connect over Wi-Fi
ts3_body:
Confirm the inventory server is on (Settings > PC Sync) and both devices are on the same network — the companion can't find a console across different Wi-Fi networks or through a guest network with client isolation.

Waking the console from sleep can take a few seconds to reconnect; give it a moment and refresh.
ts4_body: Turn on USB File Transfer in Settings > Diagnostics, then reconnect the cable — some cables are power-only. If the PC still doesn't see it, check the USB 3.0 status row in Settings > Diagnostics and try a different port.
ts5_title: Verify reports Bad or Unknown files
ts5_body: Bad means the file doesn't match its DAT checksum — a corrupted or incomplete download; re-download it. Unknown means no DAT entry matched it — the DAT set may be out of date; fetch the latest from Settings > Data Files.
ts6_body: Not every console has a DAT set available. Settings > Data Files > Manage DAT Files shows what's downloadable — if a console isn't listed there, verification isn't supported for it yet.
ts7_title: An emulator or app update failed
ts7_body: Settings > Updates > App & Emulator Updates shows the failure reason (offline, rate-limited, or no source set). Set or fix the source (X on the entry) and try again — Revert restores the previous backup if a bad install landed.
ts8_title: Running low on SD card space
ts8_body: Settings > Storage shows free space and the biggest files in your library. Turning on Keep Archives Compressed (Settings > Downloads) keeps new downloads zipped instead of extracted, trading space for a slightly longer install step.
ts9_title: An import from the PC didn't bring anything in
ts9_body: Make sure you're sending from the same screen that generated the address/code shown — it's a one-time session. If it timed out, back out and start the import again from Settings > PC Sync.
ts10_body: An update finishes installing on the next full restart, not just returning to the home menu — close HaulNX completely (hold X on it, or use the Home Menu) and relaunch it.
ts11_title: My emulator can't find my games
ts11_body:
Check Settings > Storage for the exact ROM folder path and point your emulator there — the default is sdmc:/roms/<console>, unless a custom install folder is set for that console.

A custom folder only applies to new downloads; games already installed elsewhere need moving by hand (or with Move, from a game's Options menu, if it's another console HaulNX manages).
ts12_body: Check Settings > Appearance > Box Art is turned on. If it is, run Scan for Box Art from a console's Options menu — a game with an unusual title may need a manual match from its own Options menu instead.
ts13_title: An archive downloaded but won't extract
ts13_body:
Check Settings > Storage first — a full SD card fails extraction partway through and leaves a partial file behind. Delete the partial and free up space, then re-download; a corrupted archive extracts cleanly once the download itself is good.

If it keeps failing with space to spare, turn on Keep Archives Compressed (Settings > Downloads) as a workaround and extract it yourself later with a PC archive tool.
ts14_body: GitHub caps how many unauthenticated checks HaulNX can make per hour — shared across every HaulNX user on the same public IP, so it can trigger even on a first-time check. Add a free GitHub API token in Settings > Account Credentials to raise the limit (see the credentials article), or just wait — it resets on its own within the hour.
ts15_title: Archive.org says the item needs a login
ts15_body: Some archive.org items are only downloadable to a logged-in account. Generate an Access/Secret Key pair at archive.org/account/s3.php and enter both in Settings > Account Credentials > Archive.org Credentials, then retry the download.
ts16_body:
Check Settings > Downloads for a rate limit left over from a previous session — Max Total Download Rate and Max Rate Per Download both default to unlimited, but either one being set low will cap every download.

If both are clear, run Speed Test in Settings > Diagnostics to see what your connection is actually delivering right now.
ts17_title: A file type isn't showing in Library
ts17_body: Settings > Appearance > File Extension Filter can hide specific file extensions from repository listings. Open it and check whether the master switch and the extension in question are both toggled on — turn either off to stop hiding it.
ts18_title: The first-run tour or Welcome screen won't come back
ts18_body: Both only appear automatically on a fresh install, once. Replay the guided tour any time from Settings > Help > Getting Started > Replay the Guided Tour — it ends on the same Welcome screen you saw the first time.

There's no checklist available to download automatically for this console yet. You can send one from a PC instead — Options > Receive from PC (the companion app's DAT Files tab, or a URL upload) — or copy a file by hand to:

tidy_fix_all_confirm: Fix all %d issues shown? Duplicates/orphans/clones are deleted, misfiled files are moved.

live_recv_msg: A file is arriving from the app utility over the live link.

pc_sync_body: Connect over USB, or receive a game over Wi-Fi?
usb_steps:
1.  Plug a USB-C cable from this console into your PC
2.  Keep the console in handheld mode (undocked)
3.  It appears as a drive — drag ROMs onto it
usb_wait: Waiting for a PC...   B disconnect
usb_connected: Connected to a PC   B disconnect
usb_fail: Couldn't start USB (dock the console? try handheld mode)
usb_busy_nav: Cancel the transfer first (B) to leave
install_pc_choose: How do you want to send from your PC?
emu_upd_confirm:
Update %s to v%s?

The installed app is replaced in place; the build you have now is not kept.
emu_upd_missing: Couldn't find that app on the SD card — nothing was changed.
emu_install_confirm:
Install %s v%s?

The app is added to sdmc:/switch.
updsrc_pushed: Update sources synced from the desktop.
appman_empty: Nothing here yet. Add entries from the desktop companion, then they'll show up here.
appman_list_hint: A options  Y check one  X check all  B back

appman_offline_msg: Couldn't reach GitHub — the console appears to be offline. Check your Wi-Fi connection and try again.
appman_needs_source:
%s has no update source set.

Point it at a GitHub repo (owner/name) to check for and install updates?

appman_revert_pick: Choose a stored build to restore.
appman_no_backups: No backups stored for this app yet. A backup is kept the first time you update it here.
appman_revert_notinst: This app isn't installed, so there's nothing to replace.
pcsync_push_list: Push emulator & app list repos to PC
appman_push_sent: Sent — the companion will pick up your list
appman_push_noconn: Connect the desktop companion first — either turn on the Wi-Fi inventory server and connect, or connect over USB.
